digest.component_or_area: MCP serving surface / gate execution infrastructure
propositions: MCP endpoint returned persistent HTTP 502 after kernel OOM-killed the container mid-gate, with nginx still pointing at the dead port and no failover

Memory oversubscription: 10 concurrent plan-review gates (~740 MB each) plus steady-state containers (~2.2 GB) exceed 8 GiB host; unbounded per-concurrent-read allocation (~295 MB per discovery read before fix) made concurrency fatal
Retiring an exited-but-live container while nginx still names its port converts transient crash to permanent 502; retire-sweep lacked a live-backend check in the non-running branch
No detection existed for unhealthy MCP upstream; detection gap meant 12-hour outage was discovered only by human report rather than alarm
Per-ticket full-state projection was applied after materializing all 8,879 tickets; moving projection inside reduce loop cut per-read footprint from 295 MB to 84 MB per concurrent call
System could not measure/bound concurrency or memory to recover after the incident, and no alarm watches host memory despite known oversubscription
